description: A tree of slopes, ridges, 35-40 m tall (to 50 m). Moderately buttressed (TTSM); 'grandes gambas delgadas', large thin buttresses (src 3); short buttresses sometimes reaching 3 m (Wikipedia, src 1, gives the height). Wikipedia: rounded crown, a common canopy tree. Fruit: brown, flat, obliquely obovoid-oblong one-seeded pod about 5 cm long.

season_notes.winter: Briefly leafless in the dry season. Fruiting.
season_notes.spring: In leaf. Flowering (white (small, fragrant, in subterminal panicles)).
season_notes.summer: In leaf. Flowering (white (small, fragrant, in subterminal panicles)).

range.where: Southern Pacific Costa Rica (Osa, Golfo Dulce) and Panama; Wikipedia adds the Atlantic coast of Colombia.

notes: Template shorea_leprosula: an emergent: a buttressed clear bole under an umbrella crown (light red meranti). NOT SOURCED (the template's or a default value): crown width (the template's ratio); crown depth (the template's); leaf colour (a tropical evergreen's mid green). Research notes: Leaves: one pair of leaflets (occasionally three), elliptic-lanceolate, long acuminate, leathery, 5-8 x 3-4 cm (TTSM); Wikipedia gives leaflets 5-7 x 2-3 cm. Phenology is Osa-specific: Vilchez (1997, cited in TTSM) at Mogos, Osa: intensive leaf fall Jan-Feb, leaf flush mainly Mar-Apr, flowers May-Aug (peak June), mature fruit Nov-Jan. Allen (1956, cited in TTSM): briefly deciduous late Dec/early Jan, brown leaves conspicuous before falling, new foliage almost immediately, the flushing tree visible for many kilometres (flush colour not given); flowers early Aug-Sep, fruit early Feb. Wikipedia: flowers Aug-Dec, fruit Nov-Feb. leafless_months [1] is my reading of 'briefly deciduous'; no source gives a leafless month count. Fruiting is not annual: mast crop Feb-Mar 2000 after little or no fruit 1995-1999 (src 4). Shade tolerance from src 3: high sapling survival in shade, high mortality in sun, poor regeneration in gaps (the paper does not use the word). dbh typical is the adult-population mode at Mogos (70-80 cm class, src 3); max 1 m from TTSM and Useful Tropical Plants. Height max 50 m from src 1 and src 3; TTSM 35-40 m. TTSM and Useful Tropical Plants call it deciduous. No source read names animals eating its fruit, seeds or leaves; src 4 discusses seed predation only generally.
